referralText:
Dear Dr. Chow,

Re: Morgan Tse, 41

Thank you for seeing this 41-year-old logistics supervisor with an 8-month history of low mood, poor sleep and reduced concentration following a restructuring at work. She has been off work on medical leave since October 27. Sertraline started in April, increased to 150 mg six weeks ago with partial benefit. PHQ-9 in my office 18. She drinks alcohol most evenings. No known medical conditions. BP 142/90 at last visit. Please assess and advise on management and return-to-work planning.

Thank you,
Dr. A. Patel, Family Physician
medsText:
Sertraline 150 mg PO daily (increased from 100 mg on Oct 8)
Zopiclone 7.5 mg PO at bedtime as needed
Ibuprofen 400 mg PO as needed
No known drug allergies

transcript.t: Hi Morgan. I'm the intake assistant for Dr. Chow's clinic. In your own words, what's been happening that led to this referral?

Since around March I've just been flat. Work did a big restructure, I got a bigger team with fewer people, and I couldn't keep up. I stopped sleeping properly and eventually my doctor put me off work.
That sounds like a lot to carry. When did you go off work?
End of October. So about four weeks now.
How have things been since you stopped working?
Honestly not much better. I thought rest would fix it. I'm on the couch most of the day and I feel guilty about my team.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or low for most of the day?
Most days, yes. Mornings are the worst.
Have you lost interest or enjoyment in things you usually like?
Yeah. I used to coach my son's soccer team and I've stopped going. Nothing feels fun.
How has your appetite or weight been?
Eating less. I've probably lost about 10 pounds since the summer without trying.
Have you had trouble concentrating, like reading or following a show?
Big time. I read the same email three times.
Have you had a time like this before, lasting two weeks or more?
Once, after my daughter was born, about 12 years ago. It got better on its own after a few months.
PHQ-9 completed: total 17 (Moderately severe). Item 9: Several days (1). Difficulty: Very difficult.
Thank you for filling that in. You marked having some thoughts of being better off dead. Can you tell me more about those thoughts?
Some nights I think everyone would be fine without me. I wouldn't do anything though. I'd never do that to my kids.
Have you had any thoughts of ending your life, or made any plans?
No plans. It's more like I wish I could just not wake up for a while.
Have you ever tried to end your life or hurt yourself on purpose?
No, never.
Are there any firearms in your home, or medicines saved up?
No guns. Just my regular pills in the cabinet.
Moving on to worry. Do you find yourself worrying a lot, and is it hard to stop?
Mostly about money and whether I'll have a job to go back to. I can't shut it off at night.
GAD-7 completed: total 11 (Moderate). Difficulty: Very difficult.
Have you had sudden waves of intense fear with a racing heart or trouble breathing?
No, nothing like that.
Tell me about your sleep. What's a typical night like?
I fall asleep okay because I usually have a few drinks, but I wake up at 3 and I'm up for hours.
Has anyone told you that you snore loudly, or stop breathing or gasp in your sleep?
My husband says I snore like a chainsaw, and sometimes I wake up choking.
Do you feel sleepy during the day, or nod off without meaning to?
I nod off on the couch most afternoons.
You mentioned having a few drinks. On how many days a week do you drink, and how many on a typical day?
Probably five or six nights a week, three or four beers. More on weekends.
Has that changed since this started?
Yeah, before this it was more like weekends only. I know it's not great.
Do you use cannabis or any other drugs?
No. Coffee, maybe four cups a day.
Have you seen a counsellor or been on any other mental health medicines before?
Just the sertraline. I saw a counsellor through work twice but stopped going.
Your medication list shows sertraline 150 mg daily and zopiclone as needed. Are you taking them as listed?
The sertraline yes. I haven't touched the zopiclone, it gave me a weird taste.
Any medical conditions, diagnosed or that your doctor is checking?
My doctor said my blood pressure was high last time. Nothing else.
Has anyone in your family had depression, bipolar disorder, alcohol problems or suicide?
My dad drank a lot. My mom had depression I think, she never got treated.
What does your job involve, and what has been hardest about it lately?
I supervise shipping at a distribution centre, 30 people. Planning schedules, dealing with complaints. I can't make decisions anymore and I dread the morning huddle.
Who lives with you, and who do you lean on for support?
My husband and two kids, 12 and 9. My husband is supportive but worried. I haven't told my friends.
What are you hoping to get out of seeing Dr. Chow?
I want to feel like myself again and figure out if and when I can go back to work. Maybe try a different medication.
Thank you, Morgan. That's everything for now. Dr. Chow will read this before your visit.

facts.text: Low mood since ~March after work restructure; off work since end of Oct
~10 lb unintended weight loss since summer
Prior postpartum episode ~12 y ago, remitted untreated
Passive death wish; denies intent, plan, attempts; children protective
Loud snoring, wakes choking, daytime dozing
3-4 beers 5-6 nights/wk, increased from weekends only
Not taking zopiclone (taste); told BP high

contradictions.text: Wakes up choking at night (T33) after denying sudden fear surges (T29); cause not clarified: consider sleep apnea vs nocturnal panic.
Uses alcohol to fall asleep (T31) while describing sleep onset as okay; sleep-onset difficulty may be masked by alcohol.

risk.summary: Passive death wish (wishes she could not wake up) on some nights; denies intent, plan, past attempts or self-harm; no firearms; children protective.
